en: Why was my payment declined?
tamil: என் பேமெண்ட் ஏன் நிராகரிக்கப்பட்டது?
context: Calling bank customer care.
explain: 'Why' asks the reason. 'Declined' means the payment was refused.
usage: Ask it on a helpline call when your payment fails.
leelaQ: What can be the reasons for a declined payment?
answer: The balance may be low or the network may be weak.

en: My phone recharge is due tomorrow.
tamil: என் போன் ரீசார்ஜ் நாளைக்கு முடியுது.
context: Telling a friend about a plan expiry.
explain: 'Due' means something must be paid or done by a time.
usage: Use it when you remind yourself or others about a payment date.
leelaQ: How often do you recharge your phone?
answer: I recharge it once a month.

en: Keep the receipt safe in case you need a refund.
tamil: பணம் திருப்பி வேணும்னா தேவைப்படும், ரசீதை பத்திரமா வச்சுக்கோங்க.
context: Advising a friend after buying something.
explain: 'In case' means because something may happen later.
usage: Use it when you advise a friend after a purchase.
leelaQ: Where do you keep important bills and receipts?
answer: I keep them in a file at home.

en: I checked three shops before buying this phone.
tamil: இந்த போனை வாங்கறதுக்கு முன்னாடி மூணு கடை பார்த்தேன்.
context: Telling a friend how you compared prices.
explain: 'Before buying' uses the -ing form after 'before'.
usage: Use it when you tell a friend how you found a good deal.
leelaQ: How do you find the best price for something?
answer: I compare prices in a few shops and on the internet.

en: This shop does not take credit cards.
tamil: இந்த கடையில கிரெடிட் கார்டு எடுத்துக்க மாட்டாங்க.
context: Telling a friend about a payment rule.
explain: 'Does not take' says what the shop refuses to accept.
usage: Use it to warn a friend before they shop and find no card option.
leelaQ: Do you prefer credit cards or debit cards?
answer: I prefer debit cards because I cannot overspend.

en: Can I get a printout of my bank statement?
tamil: என் வங்கி அறிக்கையை பிரிண்ட் எடுத்து தர முடியுமா?
context: Asking at the bank counter.
explain: 'Can I get ...?' is a common way to ask for a service.
usage: Ask it at the bank when you need a statement for a visa or loan.
leelaQ: When do people need a bank statement?
answer: They need it for a loan or a visa.

en: Everything is getting costlier these days.
tamil: இப்பல்லாம் எல்லாமே விலை ஏறிட்டே போகுது.
context: Complaining about prices to a neighbour.
explain: 'Getting costlier' shows a change that keeps happening.
usage: Use it in everyday talk about rising prices.
leelaQ: What has become costlier in your area?
answer: Vegetables and rent have become costlier.

en: I have applied for a home loan.
tamil: நான் வீட்டுக் கடனுக்கு விண்ணப்பிச்சிருக்கேன்.
context: Sharing news with a colleague.
explain: 'Have applied' shows you did it and are now waiting.
usage: Use it when you share a big money plan with friends or colleagues.
leelaQ: What kind of house would you like to buy?
answer: I would like a small house near my office.

en: You may get a better rate at another bank.
tamil: வேற வங்கியில இன்னும் நல்ல வட்டி கிடைக்கலாம்.
context: Giving advice to a friend about a deposit.
explain: 'May' shows a possibility, not a sure thing.
usage: Use it to suggest a friend compare banks before deciding.
leelaQ: How do you choose a bank?
answer: I check the interest rate and the nearest branch.

en: Does this bill include tax?
tamil: இந்த பில்ல வரி சேர்த்து இருக்கா?
context: Asking a cashier at a restaurant.
explain: 'Include' means the price already has the tax inside.
usage: Ask it at a restaurant or shop to understand the total price.
leelaQ: Do you read your bills before paying?
answer: Yes, I read them quickly before I pay.

en: I will ask my father before I sign anything.
tamil: எதுலயும் கையெழுத்து போடறதுக்கு முன்னாடி அப்பாகிட்ட கேட்பேன்.
context: Telling an agent you need advice first.
explain: 'Before I sign' uses the present tense after 'before' even for the future.
usage: Use it to politely slow down an agent who is in a hurry.
leelaQ: Who do you ask for advice about money?
answer: I ask my father and my elder brother.

en: Could you send me your UPI ID?
tamil: உங்க UPI ஐடி அனுப்ப முடியுமா?
context: Asking a friend for payment details.
explain: 'Could you send me ...?' is polite and short.
usage: Use it when you need to pay a friend or a seller by phone.
leelaQ: What do you need to send money to someone?
answer: I need their phone number or UPI ID.

en: My brother lent me two thousand rupees.
tamil: என் அண்ணன் எனக்கு ரெண்டாயிரம் ரூபாய் கடன் கொடுத்தார்.
context: Telling a friend how you managed a payment.
explain: 'Lent' is the past of 'lend'. Borrow and lend are opposites.
usage: Use it when you explain where you got money from.
leelaQ: Did anyone help you with money when you needed it?
answer: Yes, my brother helped me once.

en: How do I reset my net banking password?
tamil: என் நெட் பேங்கிங் பாஸ்வேர்டை எப்படி மாத்தறது?
context: Asking a bank helpdesk.
explain: 'How do I ...?' asks for the way to do something.
usage: Ask it at the bank or on a helpline when you cannot log in.
leelaQ: How do you remember all your passwords?
answer: I write hints in a safe notebook.

en: Rent takes almost half of my salary.
tamil: வாடகை என் சம்பளத்துல கிட்டத்தட்ட பாதி எடுத்துக்குது.
context: Talking about living costs in a big city.
explain: 'Takes half of my salary' means half of the money goes there.
usage: Use it when you talk about the cost of living.
leelaQ: How much of your income goes on housing?
answer: About one third of my income goes on housing.

en: I did not know about the hidden charges.
tamil: மறைமுக கட்டணங்கள் பத்தி எனக்கு தெரியாது.
context: Complaining to a service provider.
explain: 'Hidden charges' are costs nobody told you about.
usage: Use it when you complain about a surprise fee on a bill.
leelaQ: What should you do when you see a strange charge?
answer: I should ask the company to explain it.

en: She is paying the school fees at the counter.
tamil: அவங்க கவுண்டர்ல பள்ளிக் கட்டணம் கட்டிட்டு இருக்காங்க.
context: Telling someone where your wife is.
explain: Present continuous with 'is' describes something happening now.
usage: Use it when you explain where someone is right now.
leelaQ: How do parents usually pay school fees?
answer: They pay online or at the school office.

en: Please call me when the money comes.
tamil: பணம் வந்ததும் எனக்கு கூப்பிடுங்க.
context: Asking a friend to inform you.
explain: 'When' with the present tense talks about a future time.
usage: Use it when you wait for a payment and need a quick update.
leelaQ: Who do you call first when you get good news?
answer: I call my mother first.

en: The bank manager explained the loan process to us.
tamil: வங்கி மேலாளர் லோன் நடைமுறையை எங்களுக்கு விளக்கினார்.
context: Telling a friend about a bank visit.
explain: 'Explained ... to us' shows who got the explanation.
usage: Use it when you talk about a visit to the bank.
leelaQ: Have you ever met a bank manager? What did you ask?
answer: Yes, I asked about a savings scheme.

en: Will you pay by cash or by card?
tamil: ரொக்கமா கட்டுவீங்களா, கார்டா?
context: A cashier asking a customer.
explain: 'Or' gives two choices. 'By cash' and 'by card' show the method.
usage: A shop cashier asks this at the counter when billing.
leelaQ: Which is safer, cash or card?
answer: Cards are safer because we can block them if lost.

en: Online shopping often gives good cashback offers.
tamil: ஆன்லைன் ஷாப்பிங்ல அடிக்கடி நல்ல கேஷ்பேக் ஆஃபர் கிடைக்கும்.
context: Telling a friend about a saving tip.
explain: 'Often' shows how frequently something happens.
usage: Use it in chats about saving money while shopping.
leelaQ: Do you buy things online? What was your last order?
answer: Yes, my last order was a pair of shoes.

en: The price has gone up since last week.
tamil: போன வாரத்துல இருந்து விலை ஏறிடுச்சு.
context: Telling a customer about a price change.
explain: 'Since' is used with present perfect for a starting point in time.
usage: Use it when you notice prices change in shops or online.
leelaQ: Which thing became expensive recently?
answer: Tomatoes became expensive recently.

en: Could you tell me where the closest cash machine is?
tamil: பக்கத்துல கேஷ் மெஷின் எங்க இருக்குன்னு சொல்ல முடியுமா?
context: Asking a passer-by for directions to a cash machine.
explain: "Could you tell me" is polite, so the verb "is" comes after the place word.
usage: Ask it from a stranger or shopkeeper when you need cash quickly.
leelaQ: How do you find places when you are in a new city?
answer: I use a map app on my phone.

en: We should compare prices before we buy.
tamil: வாங்கறதுக்கு முன்னாடி விலைகளை ஒப்பிட்டு பார்க்கணும்.
context: Advising your sister before shopping.
explain: 'Should' gives advice. 'Compare' means look at two or more things together.
usage: Use it when you give shopping advice to family.
leelaQ: How do you decide what to buy when two things look the same?
answer: I choose the one with the better price and quality.

en: I will not buy it unless the price comes down.
tamil: விலை குறையலனா நான் இதை வாங்க மாட்டேன்.
context: Telling a seller your limit.
explain: 'Unless' means 'if not'. 'Will not' is a firm decision.
usage: Use it while bargaining at a market or shop.
leelaQ: Do you bargain in shops? Why or why not?
answer: Yes, I bargain because small shops allow it.
